notes_list.title: Reaction Sequence Questions
notes_list.basic_overview: Multi-step synthesis questions require the output of one reaction to become the substrate of the next reaction.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
Never treat each reagent independently. Draw the structure after every step. Then verify whether the next reagent reacts with the new functional group. This prevents many errors in multi-step GATE and CSIR-NET problems.

MECHANISM & STEPWISE EXPLANATION
The source describes the transformation as: Multi-step synthesis questions require the output of one reaction to become the substrate of the next reaction. The mechanism should be read as activation of the stated substrate, formation of the key reactive intermediate, the bond-making/bond-breaking event described by the reaction, and the stated work-up/product-forming step.

1. Activate the stated substrate with the listed reagent/conditions.
2. Generate the key reactive intermediate or electrophile/nucleophile implied by the reaction.
3. Carry out the characteristic bond-forming, bond-breaking or rearrangement step.
4. Complete proton transfer/work-up and verify the characteristic product.
